source.title: Copolymers at selective interfaces: settled issues and open problems

accepted.question_text: Consider the general copolymer model near a selective interface in which the renewal inter-arrival law satisfies K(n) ~ C_K / n^(1+α) and α lies in (0,1). In the weak-coupling regime the critical curve satisfies h_c(λ) ~ m_αλ as λ ↓ 0, where m_α is universal in the sense that it depends only on α and not on the detailed disorder law or on the finer details of K(·). Determine the value of m_α, or equivalently determine the correct weak-coupling slope of the critical curve.
accepted.context_brief: Universal critical slope in weak coupling

evidence.quote: What the previous results and discussion expose is that a convincing heuristic theory predicting the location of the critical curve, or just its slope at the origin, is lacking. In this sense we consider that capturing the value of mα, for α ∈ (0,1), is an important open problem.

accepted.question_text: For the copolymer model with α = 1/2, prove that the weak-coupling critical slope m_{1/2} is strictly larger than 2/3.

evidence.quote: here are two sub-problems that are open: ? show that m1/2 > 2/3;

accepted.question_text: Does there exist some α > 0 for which the weak-coupling critical slope satisfies m_α = 1/(1+α)?

evidence.quote: here are two sub-problems that are open: ? show that m1/2 > 2/3; ? is mα = 1/(1+α) for some α > 0?

accepted.question_text: For the general copolymer model, the free energy near criticality is known to satisfy F(λ, h_c(λ)+δ) ≤ (1+α)c(λ)δ^2 for every δ > 0 under the stated disorder assumptions. Can this smoothing bound be improved by replacing the exponent 2 with a larger exponent?

evidence.quote: for every λ > 0 there exists c(λ) < ∞ such that F(λ,hc(λ) +δ) ≤ (1+α)c(λ)δ2 for every δ > 0.
A natural open question however is: ? Can one improve (20), in the sense of replacing the exponent 2 with a larger value?

accepted.question_text: How does the critical behavior of the copolymer model depend on the tail exponent α and possibly also on the coupling parameter λ? In particular, determine whether the near-critical behavior is α-dependent, λ-dependent, both, or neither.
accepted.context_brief: Dependence of critical behavior on α and λ

evidence.quote: One can of course wonder whether the critical behavior of the copolymer model depends or not on α (and on λ?) and how, but once again, the substantial lack of sound physical predictions is quite disappointing.

accepted.question_text: In the localized phase, let μ(λ,h) denote the inverse correlation length defined through the exponential decay rate appearing in the model's excursion and correlation estimates. As h approaches the critical point h_c(λ) from below, is log μ(λ,h) asymptotic to log F(λ,h), where F(λ,h) is the free energy?
accepted.context_brief: Inverse correlation length versus free energy

evidence.quote: where µ is defined as µ(λ,h) = − limN→∞ 1/N log E (1+e−2λ ∑N n=1 (ωn+h)) / ZN,ω .

But: ? is it true that logµ(λ,h) ∼ log F(λ,h) as h & hc(λ)? In view of the discussion on disorder relevance in section 1.5, we expect that this is not the case and establishing such a result would be very interesting.

accepted.question_text: Let Δ_n be the indicator that the copolymer is below the interface at monomer n. If (λ,h) lies in the interior of the delocalized region D, is it true that for every ε > 0 the quenched probability P_{N,ω}(Δ_n = 0 for every n in [εN, N] ∩ ℕ) converges to 0 almost surely with respect to the disorder as N → ∞?

evidence.quote: It is mathematically useful to use the variable ∆n, that in the random walk case is just (1−sign(Sn))/2, i.e. the indicator function that the copolymer is below the axis.
For example: ? Is it true that, if (λ,h) is in the interior of D, for every ε > 0 we have limN→∞ PN,ω(∆n = 0 for every n ∈ [εN,N]∩N) = 0 P(dω)-almost surely?

needs_review.question_text_raw: Finally, it is natural to wonder what happens when a pinning interaction is added to the copolymer model... there are works on this model, often called copolymer with adsorption ..., but the understanding is very limited.

evidence.quote: Finally, it is natural to wonder what happens when a pinning interaction is added to the copolymer model, that is when not only the solvents are selective, but something special goes on at the interface ... there are works on this model, often called copolymer with adsorption ..., but the understanding is very limited.
